newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Excluded Serbs blast Bosnian aid conference.
newsitem.headline: Excluded Serbs blast Bosnian aid conference.

text.p: Bosnian Serb officials bitter at being excluded from $1.22 billion in foreign aid for 1997 said on Thursday the international community was wrong in linking financial assistance to compliance with the U.N. war crimes tribunal.

"The linking of (tribunal issues) to economic development and reconstruction is detrimental to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the buildup of peace," said a statement from the Serb delegation to an international donor conference.
On Wednesday, some 48 countries and 30 international institutions pledged $1.22 billion to aid reconstruction in Bosnia.

But the Serb Republic, the autonomous entity which splits postwar Bosnia with a Moslem-Croat federation, was denied aid until it cooperates fully with all aspects of the Dayton peace treaty that ended the 1992-95 war.
One of the key provisions is the handover of Serbs, Croats and Moslems indicted for war atrocities by the tribunal. Most of the almost 80 people under public indictment are Serbs.

Serb authorities have not delivered any indictees, which include former president Radovan Karadzic, contending they had only defended the Serb nation in war and saying that the Serb Republic constitution forbade extradition of its citizens.
The Serb statement said Serb authorities had attempted to cooperate with the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia, based in The Hague, but that the court was biased.
"The ongoing procedure on war crimes against Serb people ... is not itself sufficient to bring us to the conclusion that the tribunal is acting in a fair and objective manner."

The statement said the existence of so-called "secret indictments" was "a complete contradiction known to legal principles" and said Serb citizens had been "kidnapped" and one left to die in The Hague because of lack of medical treatment.

It said Milan Kovacevic, jailed in The Hague after his arrest by NATO troops on the basis of a sealed indictment earlier this month, was in poor health, not provided with adequate medical care and not fit to stand trial.
